title: Side B, Eleven Years
genre: upright-piano saloon torch ballad (1950s late-night lounge)
subject: a woman who still has the jazz record a man lent her eleven years ago and has never returned it, because as long as she has it he has a reason to call
caption: 1950s late-night lounge torch ballad in slow 6/8. Upright piano with slightly honky tone and sustained chords, brushed snare, upright bass walking gently, muted trumpet answering the vocal and a distant cello in the last chorus. Close-miked small-club room with soft tape saturation. Female lead, low alto, slow and fully sung with sustained notes. Clear full voice, every word enunciated, steady sung melody on every line. 66 BPM, F major. Hushed, rueful, tender mood. No drum machine, no electric guitar, no synth, no autotune, no dance beat.
lyrics:
[Intro - upright piano, brushed snare]

[Verse 1]
You lent me a record on a Friday night
Said bring it back Friday, I'll leave on the light
The sleeve has gone soft where my thumb goes
The needle still finds it with its eyes closed

[Pre-Chorus]
I've moved four times and it came with me
In a box marked kitchen, so nobody sees

[Chorus]
Side B, eleven years
Still waiting on your call
I could post it in a minute
Then you'd have no cause to call

[Verse 2]
A woman at the shop said just sell it, dear
It's worth some money, it's scratched, it's rare
I said I know what it's worth to me
It's the only Friday I keep

[Chorus]
Side B, eleven years
Still waiting on your call
I could post it in a minute
Then you'd have no cause to call

[Bridge - piano alone, trumpet enters]
If you ask me for it back
I'll say I lost it, come and look

[Chorus]
Side B, eleven years
Still waiting on your call
Come and get it, come and get it
Come and take the record back

[Outro - piano and muted trumpet, slow fade]
Bring it back Friday
I'll leave on the light
